headline: US stocks trade lower as Brent crude tops $100 on US‑Iran tensions, lifting September Fed hike odds and pushing 10‑year yields toward 4.81%
raw_text:
- S&P 500 (SPX) falls 0.28%, Dow Jones (DJI) loses 0.72%, Nasdaq 100 (NDX) slips 0.05%, and Russell 2000 (IWM) declines 0.56% amid broad equity weakness
- Brent crude (@QA) trades above $100 per barrel for the first time since July on escalating US‑Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz supply risks, stoking inflation concerns
- Fed rate‑hike expectations rise to roughly a 60% chance of a September move as higher oil weakens Treasuries and lifts the 10‑year yield near 4.81%
- Energy outperforms as Exxon Mobil (XOM) rises about 2% with higher crude supporting the broader group
- Roivant Sciences (ROIV) rises nearly 1% on positive clinical data, leading individual gainers
- Intel (INTC) rises about 1% on optimism around AI infrastructure demand
- Health care, consumer discretionary, and industrials lag, with notable decliners including Novartis (NVS) which trades higher after priority review for Duchenne drug and Deere (DE) which trades roughly flat post‑earnings
- Additional underperformers include Howmet Aerospace (HWM) down 0.21%, Amgen (AMGN) up 0.24%, Dyne Therapeutics (DYN) down 1.67%, and Stryker (SYK) up 0.27%
- Chewy (CHWY) declines about 6% after beating Q2 estimates with EPS of $0.36 and lifting full-year outlook, while ODDITY Tech (ODD) advances on its earnings release
- Signet Jewelers (SIG) rises after a 26.6% EPS beat to $2.19, whereas Casey’s General Stores (CASY) falls over 18% despite an earnings beat driven by fuel margins as inside same‑store sales growth slows to 3.2%
